paper_title: Direct Detection of Dark Photon Dark Matter with the James Webb Space Telescope
coupling_convention: epsilon x (rho_A'/rho_DM)^0.5, dimensionless kinetic mixing scaled by DM density fraction, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper proposes DPDM detection with a MODIFIED JWST mirror configuration during ground testing (applicable to future space telescopes like LUVOIR, HabEx, Origins, Roman). The current in-space JWST configuration cannot detect DPDM-induced photons, so the epsilon curve in Fig. 4 is a projected sensitivity, not an observed limit. Only summary values available in text: epsilon ~ 1e-12 to 1e-14 over 10-500 THz (m_A' ~ 0.041-2.07 eV) at 95% CL. The two data points encode this range assuming sensitivity improves toward higher frequency; the actual curve shape (red dashed in Fig. 4, split between NIRSpec and MIRI bands) is not numerically recoverable from the text. Local DM density value not explicitly stated in the provided content (uses rho_DM symbolically with Standard Halo Model, v0=235 km/s, vesc~500 km/s). | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 4 shows 95% C.L. projected sensitivity for dark photon dark matter with JWST. The red dashed curve has two sections: JWST-MIRI (0.04-0.235 eV, sensitivity ~3e-13) and JWST-NIR (0.235-2.1 eV, sensitivity ~2e-14 to 1e-13). The curve is jagged (many narrow spikes from spectral features around 0.85-1.2 eV and near 2 eV); I traced the effective envelope of the dashed boundary. Sharp transition at ~0.235 eV between MIRI and NIRSpec sections. Steep vertical rise at left edge (~0.042 eV) and rise at right edge (~2.05 eV) where sensitivity terminates. Y-axis is epsilon x (rho_A'/rho_DM)^0.5, equal to epsilon when dark photons constitute all local DM.
